question: Which customers are exposed if supplier S-104 misses its next ship date? Show the affected products and the top 10 accounts and payers by volume on them.
answer:
If S-104 (Delmar Specialty Chemicals, a tier-2 supplier in India) misses its next ship date, all prescriptions for the three Lacrivia/Cyclosporine eye-drop packs are exposed: 13,986 TRx in the last 13 weeks. Eight health systems and two independent clinics account for 80.5% of that volume, and the top 10 payers account for 80.0%.

**What's at risk**
- **The next shipment:** order PO005791 for 4,200 units of RM-221 (Polysorbate 80, low-peroxide), promised to ship **2026-10-07**. S-104's other material, RM-222, doesn't ship again until 2026-10-26.
- **No backup supplier:** S-104 is the only approved source for RM-221. The alternate, S-131, isn't qualified. The next step up (CMP-310, a premix made by S-201) also has only one supplier.
- **Recovery takes about 50 days:** that's the time from RM-221 arriving until finished Lacrivia 5 mL reaches the distribution centre (DC). It includes a 14-day sterility test, so every day of delay pushes the recovery date back.

**Affected products (current bill of materials only)**
| Product | NDC | TRx, last 13 weeks |
|---|---|---|
| Lacrivia 0.1% emulsion 5 mL (FG-1001) | 99101-0101-05 | 7,017 |
| Lacrivia 0.1% emulsion 10 mL (FG-1002) | 99101-0101-10 | 3,425 |
| Cyclosporine 0.05% emulsion 5 mL (FG-1003) | 99101-0202-05 | 3,544 |
| Lens care solutions 1–11 (FG-3001 to FG-3011) | 99101-40xx | Not in the commercial database; no customer view |

**Top 10 customers by TRx on these three packs (weeks ending 2026-07-03 to 2026-09-25)**
| # | Customer | Type | Supply contract tier | TRx | Share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Oak Hollow Health System | Health system | A | 1,731 | 12.4% |
| 2 | Riverbend Health System | Health system | A | 1,609 | 11.5% |
| 3 | Northfield Health System | Health system | A | 1,532 | 11.0% |
| 4 | Sunridge Health System | Health system | B | 1,511 | 10.8% |
| 5 | Brightwater Health System | Health system | – | 1,418 | 10.1% |
| 6 | Stonegate Health System | Health system | – | 1,200 | 8.6% |
| 7 | Clearview Health System | Health system | B (expires 2026-12-31) | 1,068 | 7.6% |
| 8 | Willow Creek Health System | Health system | – | 701 | 5.0% |
| 9 | Sunridge Vision Associates 20 | Independent clinic | – | 248 | 1.8% |
| 10 | Glenmoor Vision Associates 12 | Independent clinic | – | 246 | 1.8% |

If supply runs short, units go first to Tier A (Oak Hollow, Riverbend, Northfield), then Tier B (Sunridge, Clearview). Everyone else is split in proportion to their last-13-week TRx.

**Top 10 payers by TRx on these three packs**
| # | Payer | TRx | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Northstar Health | 1,635 | 11.7% |
| 2 | Bluecrest Mutual | 1,630 | 11.7% |
| 3 | Silverline Health | 1,427 | 10.2% |
| 4 | Harborview Health | 1,274 | 9.1% |
| 5 | Redwood Benefit Trust | 1,030 | 7.4% |
| 6 | Pinnacle Benefit Group | 926 | 6.6% |
| 7 | Lakeshore Health | 915 | 6.5% |
| 8 | Keystone Medical Plan | 802 | 5.7% |
| 9 | Meadowbrook Care | 775 | 5.5% |
| 10 | Cash / Discount Card | 771 | 5.5% |

Cash / Discount Card isn't an insurer. The next insured payer is Granite Plains Health (735).

**Sources and definitions**
- **Supply side:** the approved supplier-to-finished-good path through the bill of materials (superseded recipes excluded; one ended link from RM-221 to CMP-320 was ignored). Tables: PURCH_ORD and SUPPLIER_MATERIAL in Fabric.
- **Customer side:** the approved product-to-customers-and-payers path in Snowflake: weekly prescriptions (RXT_WKLY) linked to prescribers, accounts and the payer list (PAYER_SPINE).
- **"Customer":** the top-level contracted account (business rule BR-CUST-01). Clinics and hospitals are rolled up to their health system; independent clinics stand on their own.
- **Other rules and data:** shortage allocation (BR-ALLOC-01), recovery lead time (BR-LEAD-01), the supply contract list, and standard manufacturing times.
- **Policy check:** passed for the SUPPLY_PLANNER role, with no masking. The decision was logged (trace b7600707).

**Assumptions**
- **"Next ship date":** the open S-104 order with the earliest promised ship date.
- **"Volume":** TRx over the 13 most recent weeks.
- **Sunridge and Glenmoor Vision Associates:** they have no parent account in the data, so I treated them as independent. That's why Sunridge Vision Associates 20 appears separately from Sunridge Health System.
- **Lead time:** the 50-day figure is for Lacrivia 5 mL. The other packs follow similar paths, but I didn't pull their times.

sql.sql: SELECT s.*, sm.MATERIAL_ID, sm.QUALIFIED_FLG, m.MATERIAL_TYP FROM dbo.SUPPLIER s LEFT JOIN dbo.SUPPLIER_MATERIAL sm ON sm.SUPPLIER_ID=s.SUPPLIER_ID LEFT JOIN dbo.MATERIAL m ON m.MATERIAL_ID=sm.MATERIAL_ID WHERE s.SUPPLIER_ID='S-104'

SELECT PO_ID, MATERIAL_ID, ORDER_DT, PROMISED_SHIP_DT, ACTUAL_SHIP_DT, QTY, STATUS FROM dbo.PURCH_ORD WHERE SUPPLIER_ID='S-104' AND (ACTUAL_SHIP_DT IS NULL OR STATUS <> 'CLOSED' OR PROMISED_SHIP_DT >= '2026-09-01') ORDER BY PROMISED_SHIP_DT

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13)
SELECT r.PROD_NDC11, COUNT(DISTINCT r.WK_END_DT) weeks, MIN(r.WK_END_DT) first_wk, MAX(r.WK_END_DT) last_wk, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) trx_13w,
 SUM(CASE WHEN p.ACCOUNT_ID IS NULL THEN r.TRX_QTY ELSE 0 END) trx_no_acct
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wk ON r.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON p.PRSCRBR_ME=r.PRSCRBR_ME
WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110','99101020205')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT a1.ACCT_TYP t1, a2.ACCT_TYP t2, a3.ACCT_TYP t3, a4.ACCT_TYP t4, COUNT(*) n
FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a1
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a2 ON a2.ACCOUNT_ID=a1.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a3 ON a3.ACCOUNT_ID=a2.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a4 ON a4.ACCOUNT_ID=a3.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY n DESC

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
rx AS (SELECT r.* FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wk ON r.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
       WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110','99101020205'))
SELECT COALESCE(a3.ACCOUNT_ID,a2.ACCOUNT_ID,a1.ACCOUNT_ID) top_acct_id,
       COALESCE(a3.ACCOUNT_NM,a2.ACCOUNT_NM,a1.ACCOUNT_NM) top_acct_nm,
       COALESCE(a3.ACCT_TYP,a2.ACCT_TYP,a1.ACCT_TYP) top_acct_typ,
       SUM(rx.TRX_QTY) trx_13w,
       SUM(CASE WHEN rx.PROD_NDC11='99101010105' THEN rx.TRX_QTY ELSE 0 END) lac_5ml,
       SUM(CASE WHEN rx.PROD_NDC11='99101010110' THEN rx.TRX_QTY ELSE 0 END) lac_10ml,
       SUM(CASE WHEN rx.PROD_NDC11='99101020205' THEN rx.TRX_QTY ELSE 0 END) cyclo_5ml,
       ROUND(100*SUM(rx.TRX_QTY)/SUM(SUM(rx.TRX_QTY)) OVER (),1) pct
FROM rx JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p ON p.PRSCRBR_ME=rx.PRSCRBR_ME
JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a1 ON a1.ACCOUNT_ID=p.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a2 ON a2.ACCOUNT_ID=a1.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.ACCOUNT a3 ON a3.ACCOUNT_ID=a2.PARENT_ACCOUNT_ID
GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY trx_13w DESC LIMIT 12

WITH wk AS (SELECT DISTINCT WK_END_DT FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY ORDER BY WK_END_DT DESC LIMIT 13),
rx AS (SELECT r.* FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r JOIN wk ON r.WK_END_DT=wk.WK_END_DT
       WHERE r.PROD_NDC11 IN ('99101010105','99101010110','99101020205'))
SELECT ps.PAYER_ID, ps.PAYER_NM, SUM(rx.TRX_QTY) trx_13w,
       SUM(CASE WHEN rx.PROD_NDC11='99101010105' THEN rx.TRX_QTY ELSE 0 END) lac_5ml,
       SUM(CASE WHEN rx.PROD_NDC11='99101010110' THEN rx.TRX_QTY ELSE 0 END) lac_10ml,
       SUM(CASE WHEN rx.PROD_NDC11='99101020205' THEN rx.TRX_QTY ELSE 0 END) cyclo_5ml,
       ROUND(100*SUM(rx.TRX_QTY)/SUM(SUM(rx.TRX_QTY)) OVER (),1) pct,
       SUM(CASE WHEN ps.PLAN_ID IS NULL THEN rx.TRX_QTY END) unmatched
FROM rx LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PAYER_SPINE ps ON ps.PLAN_ID=rx.PLAN_ID
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY trx_13w DESC LIMIT 12
